newsitem.title: UK: Breakthrough seen close on EU links with Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Breakthrough seen close on EU links with Jordan.

text.p: The European Union said on Wednesday it was close to achieving a breakthrough with Jordan in negotiations towards an association accord that paves the way for membership of an eventual free trade zone.

European Commission vice-president Manuel Marin told reporters at a conference on investment in the Mediterranean region that negotiations with Jordan were well advanced and that an informal agreement could be reached on the margins of the meeting.
"I hope to conclude this today if possible with Jordan," he said, after speaking at a news conference also attended by Jordan's Crown Prince El-Hassan bin Talal.
"We have to see whether we can find solutions to one or two problems. If we are able, probably we can conclude immediately -- negotiations with Jordan are very, very advanced."
He declined to comment on what any sticking points might be, but political analysts say the status and movement of illegal workers, mainly Palestinians, was the thorniest issue.
But El-Hassan said he was confident agreement could be reached soon.
"There are no outstanding points of any weight," he said, when asked what stumbling blocks remained.
"We have spoken about agricultural production, intellectual property rights and all of these issues are resolvable," he said.

"Of course as far as the issue of third country nationals is concerned, Jordan is a country that has been host to massive immigrations in 1848, 1967 and 1990, therefore this issue certainly has to be addressed in terms of its legal and social contexts," he said.

Marin said the EU, which has already concluded association accords with Tunisia, Morocco, Israel, and most recently the Palestinian National Authority, intended to conclude one with Egypt within the next two weeks.
"Probably before March 24, in two weeks, we will conclude with Egypt," he said, adding the EU had held productive discussions with Lebanon this week and talks were underway with Algeria.
Association accords offer their signatories financial, social and cultural links with the EU and are seen as a stepping stone towards a free trade zone with the 15-nation European bloc.
